newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians downbeat on talks with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians downbeat on talks with Israel.

text.p: Palestinians on Tuesday said Israel opened U.S.-brokered talks on troop redeployment in the West Bank city of Hebron with proposals that threaten to push the peace process back into crisis.

Palestinians said face-to-face negotiations on Monday, the first to discuss the long-delayed reduction of Israeli troops in the Arab city since clashes that killed 59 Palestinians and 15 Israelis, lasted only 15 minutes.
Israeli security sources said it was 30 minutes but an official spokesman said it was "considerably longer".

"The Israeli side is still working to cancel the agreement, which threatens to undermine the whole peace process," Palestinian negotiator Hassan Asfour told Reuters. "It seems the Israelis did not understand or have not understood the political explosion yet."
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told reporters in Gaza asking about the Monday negotiations: "I'm sorry it was not positive but we hope something new will happen today."

But elsewhere there appeared to be an easing of the tension that has gripped the area since clashes were triggered by Israel's opening of an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem last month.
Arafat was to make his first public visit to the Jewish state for a meeting later on Tuesday in the seaside Israeli town of Caesarea with President Ezer Weizman.
Arafat's only previous visit to Israel -- at night and without advance announcement -- was a condolence call on the widow of assassinated prime minister Yitzhak Rabin last November in Tel Aviv.

Israel also lifted its military blockade of the West Bank town of Ramallah, north of Jerusalem. Israel has lifted closures of most West Bank towns since the Israeli-Palestinian summit in Washington last week led to renewed Israeli-Palestinian talks.

Palestinians looked to the talks at Erez on the Israeli-Gaza border as the chief barometer of progress on the peace process begun by the Israeli government defeated by hardline Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in elections last May.

The United States, which is brokering the ongoing talks, urged quick progress as negotiations opened on Monday on implementing the agreement to redeploy Israeli troops in the city of 100,000 Arabs and 400 militant Jewish settlers.
"The Israelis yesterday showed a position which completely contradicts the agreement," Asfour said. "Yesterday, a sharp crisis happened and the session of the talk lasted for only 15 minutes."
U.S. Special Middle East Peace Envoy Dennis Ross, mediating at the talks, said in a statement the talks were "serious and businesslike."

Israeli security sources said Israel suggested modifications to an existing Hebron pullback plan to safeguard Jewish enclaves in the centre of the city. The agreement was due to have been implemented nearly seven months ago.

The sources said Israel proposed keeping troops on hills overlooking the city centre, limiting weapons for Palestinian police in Hebron and creating buffer zones dividing Israeli troops from PLO police in the city.

"It is possible to say that there were no negotiations yesterday," said Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat. "They (Israelis) tried to discuss general principles outside the framework of the agreement but we rejected this."
